meta.document: LadhaQuest Master Blueprint: African Kitchen Intelligence Platform
synthesised_from: Report 4: Competitive audit (UI, discovery, regional tagging, creator tools, SEO)
meta.mission: Do not merely add more recipes. Make every recipe actionable in a real African kitchen: discover, plan, shop, cook, learn, share.
meta.positioning_statement: LadhaQuest is the African Kitchen Intelligence Platform: the only recipe product that understands local ingredient names, local availability, local prices and local substitutions across 54 African countries and the diaspora.
how_to_use_in_cursor: Save as ladhaquest_master_blueprint.cursor.json at the repo root.
FIRST inspect the existing codebase (framework, routing, DB, search, structured data) and write docs/AUDIT.md. Do not assume the stack in this file; reconcile it with what exists.
Execute one sprint at a time from roadmap.sprint_1_task_list, then the phases in order.
Use the cursor_prompts section as ready-made prompts.
Every task must meet global_definition_of_done before moving on.

assumptions_and_reconciliation.research_limitations: Live fetch of ladhaquest.com was blocked by robots.txt, so site facts come from the four supplied reports (themselves based on public pages). Cursor must validate every claim against the real codebase and analytics.

data_conflicts_to_resolve.issue: Recipe count differs: 2,100+ (homepage claim) vs 1,700+ (recipe index claim).
data_conflicts_to_resolve.action: Query the production DB for the true published count; use the real number in schema, UI and KPIs.

data_conflicts_to_resolve.issue: Competitor claims (Allrecipes 51K+ recipes, 7M+ reviews; African Food Network Africooks) are third-party observations.
data_conflicts_to_resolve.action: Treat as benchmarks only; never copy competitor content.

data_conflicts_to_resolve.issue: Market-size claims (e.g. South Africa, Nigeria, Kenya, Egypt = 65-70% of African food-delivery value) are unverified here.
data_conflicts_to_resolve.action: Verify with a current source before using in any investor or marketing material.

corrections_to_source_reports.problem: dietConflict checks whether candidate.dietTags INCLUDES any of the user's required diet tags and then rejects. That rejects compatible candidates (a vegan user would reject vegan substitutes).
corrections_to_source_reports.fix: Reject when the candidate does NOT satisfy every required diet tag: requiredDiets.every(d => candidate.dietTags.includes(d)). Also check religious/halal/kosher flags and meat/dairy derived tags.

corrections_to_source_reports.problem: INNER JOIN on ingredient_availability drops curated substitutes with no availability row.
corrections_to_source_reports.fix: LEFT JOIN and treat missing availability as unknown (score 0.3, flagged 'availability unverified') instead of excluding; apply the hard availability cutoff only when data exists for that country.

corrections_to_source_reports.problem: Contains 'ground_cashew paste' (space, not a slug) and ids that are slugs rather than UUIDs.
corrections_to_source_reports.fix: Allowlist must contain real ingredient slugs/UUIDs validated against the DB; reject any LLM output id not in the allowlist.
The hard filter must catch it; for vegan/dairy-free users suggest cashew/groundnut cream or blended coconut flesh.

corrections_to_source_reports.problem: Local names are not one-to-one. 'Morogo' (Southern Africa) is a family of leafy greens, not a synonym for sukuma wiki. 'Sukuma wiki' may be kale or collards depending on region.
corrections_to_source_reports.fix: Model aliases as many-to-many (alias -> ingredient with a match_confidence and an ambiguity flag). When an alias maps to several ingredients, the resolver must ask the user or use recipe/country context to disambiguate. Also treat 'ndizi' as banana (Swahili), a different thing from plantain in some markets.

corrections_to_source_reports.problem: Open Food Facts is ODbL (share-alike and attribution obligations); FAO and national tables have varying licences.
corrections_to_source_reports.fix: Keep imported datasets in separate tables with licence metadata; legal review before merging ODbL data into a proprietary database that is redistributed.
Re-score after a measured audit (Lighthouse, Search Console, GA4).

executive_summary.thesis: Allrecipes wins on scale and community; African Food Network wins on heritage and contributor identity; no one wins on African cooking utility. LadhaQuest can own that gap by combining its country/region taxonomy with a proprietary African Ingredient Graph, a safe hybrid substitution engine, budget-aware planning, and an attribution-first creator program, all on top of technically excellent recipe SEO.

substitution_engine.design_principle: Curated graph is the source of truth. AI never invents or ranks substitutions; it explains and adapts quantities from an allowlist supplied by retrieval.
pipeline: 1. Normalise input (text, locale, recipe context) and resolve ingredient via alias table (country/language aware, disambiguate if ambiguous)

2. Retrieve candidates in layers: (a) curated direct, (b) functional equivalents by function_tags, (c) semantic candidates via embeddings and co-occurrence (flagged lower trust, never marked verified)
3. Apply hard filters: allergens, diet/religious (halal, vegan, vegetarian, gluten-free, etc.), food safety, cooking-method incompatibility, availability (only when data exists)
5. LLM step: explain and adapt quantities/cooking notes using ONLY allowlisted IDs; validate JSON schema and IDs; fall back to template explanation on failure
6. Return ranked results with confidence, impact labels and warnings; cache by (ingredient, country, diet-hash, method)

signals.D: Dietary/allergy compatibility beyond hard filters (e.g. preferences)

scoring.tuning: Weights are configurable and re-fitted from feedback in Phase 4; keep an offline evaluation set of 300 expert-labelled substitution cases.

confidence_bands.low: < 0.65 (never present as exact replacement; always show tradeoff)

api.rate_limit: per IP and per user; cache hot queries in Redis (TTL 24h, invalidate on substitution edits)

llm_guardrails: Provide allowed_candidate_ids; reject any output ID not in the list
Strict JSON schema validation (Zod); on failure, retry once then fall back to templated explanation
No invented nutrition facts; nutrition only from verified DB fields
Always surface allergen/food-safety warnings from DB, not from the model
Log prompt version, model, input hash, output and validation result to ai_audit_log
Temperature low; max tokens capped; cost budget per request
Prompt-injection hygiene: treat user text and recipe text as data, never instructions
quality_controls: Human culinary reviewer approves every substitution before is_verified=true
Separate direct, functional and emergency types in UI
Show confidence, flavor impact, texture impact, cooking adjustments
'Worked / didn't work' feedback loop on every suggestion
AI-proposed substitutions stored as proposed, never auto-published

JSON-LD: Recipe (name, image[], author, datePublished, description, recipeCuisine, recipeCategory, keywords, recipeIngredient, recipeInstructions as HowToStep, prepTime, cookTime, totalTime, recipeYield, nutrition, video where present), Person (authors, sameAs), Organization, WebSite with SearchAction, BreadcrumbList (Home > Country > Region > Dish > Recipe), FAQPage only where visible FAQs exist, ItemList on collection hubs

Faceted URL governance: indexable allow-list = single-facet combos with demand (country, country+meal type, country+diet, ingredient). All other combinations noindex,follow or canonicalised; param order normalised; no infinite combinations; robots.txt blocks crawl traps (sort, page>N variants as appropriate)
XML sitemaps split by type (recipes, hubs, glossary, creators, images), lastmod accurate, hreflang when translations launch
Image SEO: descriptive filenames, alt text, srcset, AVIF/WebP, lazy loading below the fold, explicit width/height
Core Web Vitals targets (mobile, p75): LCP < 2.5 s, INP < 200 ms, CLS < 0.1; budget JS per template
Clean 301s, no redirect chains, custom 404 with search, pagination with crawlable links

content_architecture.programmatic_quality_gate: A generated hub/substitution page is published only if it has unique editorial intro, at least N (e.g. 5) relevant recipes or verified substitutes, and passes duplicate-content checks.

Licence field per source, legal review, separable ODbL data
Regional reviewers, contributor attribution, corrections policy
Guided tooling, revenue share, partnerships with cooks and food historians, family-recipe campaigns
Timestamps and confidence, crowd verification, show 'estimated'

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Scope creep into commerce too early

risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Narrow tasks, caching, cost caps, schema validation, fallbacks
Performance budgets, PWA caching, image optimisation, CI enforcement

global_definition_of_done: Code reviewed, typed, linted; unit and e2e tests pass in CI
Mobile-first verified on a throttled mid-range Android profile
Accessibility checks pass (axe plus manual spot checks)
Lighthouse and CWV budgets met on affected templates
Structured data valid and canonical/indexation rules verified for new pages
Provenance, licence and review_status present on all new data records
No fabricated ratings, reviews, nutrition or credentials
guardrails: Do not scrape competitor content or reproduce copyrighted recipes
Use original, contributor-owned or properly licensed media
Do not fabricate ratings, reviews, nutrition data, or author credentials
Require editorial or community review for culturally sensitive origin, naming and regional claims
AI proposes, humans approve; the LLM never invents substitution IDs or overwrites authoritative data
Validate every instruction here against the real codebase before implementing; do not invent unsupported capabilities
final_principle: Do not merely add more recipes. Make every recipe actionable in a real African kitchen.
